cases.name: Santa Fe Independent School District v. Doe

components.decision: The Court invalidated the school’s student-led, student-selected prayer policy before football games.
components.scope: The school policy and public-address setting mattered; this was not a ban on students praying privately.
components.survey_fit: The question names student-led prayer, school-sponsored events, the public-address system and football games. This is closer than graduation prayer, but omits Santa Fe’s election procedure and full school policy; it remains contextual rather than ruling approval.

observations.wording: Allowing students to lead prayer over the public-address system at school-sponsored events, including football games.
observations.wording_note: Paraphrased summary. University of Connecticut conducted the survey. Methodology is on printed pages 35–37. The question names school sponsorship, student leadership and the public-address setting, but not Santa Fe’s election procedure or full policy. Published categories total 101% through rounding; not renormalized.
observations.weight: Published weighted national telephone-survey topline; no respondent-level recalculation.
observations.denominator: Item sample of 1,015 adults, including uncertainty/nonresponse. Published percentages retained.
observations.orientation: Policy preference only; not approval of the full holding or constitutional reasoning.

cases.name: Good News Club v. Milford Central School

components.issue: Religious viewpoint in an after-school forum
components.decision: Excluding the club because of its religious viewpoint violated the Free Speech Clause.
components.scope: Access for a private club in a limited public forum, not school-led religious instruction.
components.locator: Syllabus, holdings 1–2; Thomas opinion, Parts II–IV.
components.survey_fit: Pew separately asks about student religious groups and religious groups generally; Gallup provides another student-group question. General-group wording avoids assuming a student-led club, but none specifies adult leadership, elementary-age children, parental permission or the full forum rules. Not objecting to access is not the same as requiring it constitutionally.

observations.wording: Allowing student religious groups to use school facilities after hours.
observations.wording_note: Paraphrased question. Article reports the full national sample of 1,016 adults. This later pre-ruling observation supersedes the 1999 after-hours question for Good News Club.
observations.denominator: National sample of 1,016 adults; original response shares retained.
observations.orientation: Policy context only; not approval of the specific holding.

observations.wording: Whether respondents would object to public schools providing after-hours facilities for student religious groups or organizations.
observations.wording_note: Paraphrased summary. Split-form item base, not the full 2,041-person survey. The full national sample includes an African-American oversample and is weighted. The two forms are parts of one survey, not independent replications. Neither specifies adult leadership, children aged 6–12, parental permission or the limited-public-forum conditions. Not objecting is not a claim that access must be constitutionally required.
observations.weight: Published weighted national telephone-survey topline; no respondent-level recalculation.
observations.denominator: Item sample of 1,023 adults, including uncertainty/nonresponse. Published percentages retained.
observations.orientation: Policy preference only; not approval of the full holding or constitutional reasoning.
